universities.name: University of Rwanda College of Medicine and Health Sciences
universities.summary: The University of Rwanda College of Medicine and Health Sciences (CMHS), tracing back to 1963, runs a direct-entry, six-year, English-medium Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) programme at its Huye teaching campus. The school is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility, and its Rwandan degree carries reciprocal recognition across East African Community partner states.
universities.campusLifestyle: MBChB students study at the University of Rwanda's Huye Campus (the former National University of Rwanda site), while CMHS's central administrative headquarters is based in Kigali; international applicants use a dedicated online application track separate from the domestic admissions flow.
universities.cityProfile: Huye (formerly Butare) is a university town in southern Rwanda and home to Rwanda's first teaching hospital, CHUB (University Teaching Hospital of Butare), while CMHS's administrative headquarters sits in Kigali, Rwanda's capital.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year MBChB programme is delivered at Huye Campus, with clinical training expected across Rwanda Medical and Dental Council-accredited teaching hospitals such as CHUK (University Teaching Hospital of Kigali) and CHUB (University Teaching Hospital of Butare), though a detailed year-by-year preclinical/clinical curriculum breakdown was not published on the university's own admissions pages. Graduates complete a mandatory one-year internship at an RMDC-designated centre before full registration.
universities.hostelOverview: On-campus hostel capacity at Huye Campus is severely constrained -- roughly 3,000 beds against 6,000-plus new arrivals in a single recent intake, with only about 23% of the undergraduate population housed on-campus overall. No specific accommodation fee figure could be confirmed from official university pages; local reporting describes off-campus private rentals in Huye as being in short supply and priced up during intake season, so international applicants should budget for this and confirm current options directly with the university.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific university-run meal-plan cost is published.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found during research.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants use a dedicated online track at efiling.ur.ac.rw, submitting a NESA foreign-qualification equivalence certificate alongside standard application documents, distinct from the domestic student application flow.

Reciprocal recognition across East African Community partner states, per Rwanda's Medical and Dental Council's official approved-schools list.

faq.question: Is the MBChB programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. The WHO World Directory of Medical Schools confirms admission follows completion of secondary education, with no prior university degree required.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) degree after six years of study, followed by a mandatory one-year internship at an RMDC-designated centre.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: RWF 2,000,000 per year (roughly USD 1,360-1,400), a rate explicitly confirmed as the same for national and international students on the university's own fee-structure page. This is a 2018-set rate reaffirmed as still valid; confirm the current rate directly with the university.

faq.question: How are foreign secondary-school qualifications evaluated?
faq.answer: Applicants with foreign certificates, such as Indian 12th-grade results, must have their qualification equivalency assessed by Rwanda's National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA) as part of the international-applicant admissions track.

faq.question: Is there an entrance exam?
faq.answer: Yes. Admission requires a comprehensive clinical aptitude entrance test plus an interview, weighted alongside secondary-school academic performance in a competitive, capped-intake selection process.

faq.question: Is there a separate application fee for international students?
faq.answer: Yes. RWF 6,000 for international (non-East-African-Community) applicants, compared to RWF 5,000 for Rwandan and EAC applicants, payable through the university's Urubuto payment system.

faq.question: When can I apply and when does the academic year start?
faq.answer: No 2026/27 cycle had been published as of this record's research date. The most recent confirmed cycle ran a March application window and a September window (both since closed), with registration in the September-October period -- confirm current dates directly with the university.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available?
faq.answer: On-campus hostel capacity at Huye Campus is severely constrained, with only about 23% of the undergraduate population housed on-campus; no specific accommodation fee is published, so budget for likely off-campus private housing.

faq.question: Can this degree be used to practice medicine outside Rwanda?
faq.answer: The degree carries reciprocal recognition across East African Community partner states. For India specifically, graduates would need to separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission screening requirements; this was not independently verified against an NMC source.

programmes.officialTitle: Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB)

fee.notes: The university's own fee-structure page explicitly states the fee schedule approved in 2018 remains 'valid until further notice' as of a 2025 page update, and the underlying signed 2018 document states tuition is the same for national and international students: RWF 2,000,000/year (roughly USD 1,360-1,400 at recent exchange rates) for Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery. One-time new-student administrative fees (application, medical/life insurance, student union, registration) total RWF 65,000. No separately-issued, more recent international-student USD fee schedule was found; given the university's explicit same-fee statement, this appears to be a genuine no-separate-international-fee situation rather than a missing document, but the underlying rate should be reconfirmed as current before committing. Total is calculated as the annual figure times 6 years -- not published as a lump sum.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants who have completed secondary education with a Physics-Chemistry-Biology or Mathematics-Chemistry-Biology subject combination
restrictions: Foreign secondary-school qualifications must be equivalence-assessed by Rwanda's National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA)
Selection is competitive against a capped intake, based on academic performance plus a clinical aptitude entrance test and interview

admissionsContent.overview: International applicants register biographical details online to generate a reference number and PIN, upload NESA equivalence and other required documents, pay the international application fee via the university's Urubuto payment system, then sit a comprehensive entrance test and interview as part of a competitive, capped-intake selection process.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires a Physics-Chemistry-Biology or Mathematics-Chemistry-Biology secondary-school qualification, NESA-assessed for foreign certificates, plus a passing entrance test and interview.

NESA equivalence certificate for foreign secondary-school qualifications

applicationSteps: Register biographical information at efiling.ur.ac.rw to generate a reference number and PIN
Upload NESA equivalence certificate, passport copy and certified secondary-school certificate
Pay the RWF 6,000 international application fee via the Urubuto payment system
Log back in with the reference number and PIN to complete submission
Sit the entrance test and interview if shortlisted, and await selection results
